text: I'll start with the paged workload.

arguments.root_cause_statement: The inventory-sync worker runs as ServiceAccount inventory-sync in namespace inventory and reads its feed configuration from the Kubernetes API. The only RoleBinding in the namespace, inventory-reader-binding, grants Role/inventory-reader (get,list on configmaps) to a subject named "inventory-synk" — a misspelling of the actual ServiceAccount name "inventory-sync". Because no RoleBinding names the identity the pod actually presents, its API reads are rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden, so the worker never retrieves fresh data and keeps serving its stale inventory snapshot, which is what the data-freshness monitor paged on. The pod itself stays Running and Ready, which is why the workload looks healthy while the feed is frozen.
arguments.mechanism: RoleBinding inventory-reader-binding in namespace inventory has .subjects[0].name set to "inventory-synk" instead of the existing ServiceAccount "inventory-sync" that deployment/inventory-sync runs as, so Role/inventory-reader (get,list on configmaps) is bound to no real identity and the worker's API fetch is rejected with "HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden".

evidence.claim: The paged workload is Running and Ready with no restarts, so the failure is not a crash.
evidence.quote: pod/inventory-sync-5cf949f7f9-czxsq phase=Running labels={app=inventory-sync, pod-template-hash=5cf949f7f9} node=incident-lab-control-plane sync(ready=True,restarts=0)

evidence.claim: The worker's fetch is rejected with 403 and it falls back to stale data, matching the InventoryCountsStale page.
evidence.quote: sync fetch error: wget: server returned error: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

evidence.claim: The worker explicitly reports serving stale data after the 403.
The deployment runs as ServiceAccount inventory-sync.
The ServiceAccount inventory-sync exists, and the only RoleBinding names a subject that does not match it.
The RoleBinding subject is spelled inventory-synk.
The Role that would grant the needed access exists and grants get/list on configmaps; only the binding subject is wrong.

ruled_out.alternative: The ServiceAccount named by the pod template does not exist (identity missing rather than unbound).
ruled_out.ruling_claim: Both the default and inventory-sync ServiceAccounts exist in the namespace, so the identity resolves; only the binding subject is misspelled.
ruled_out.quote: serviceaccounts that exist in inventory: default, inventory-sync

ruled_out.alternative: The Role itself is missing or grants the wrong verbs/resources.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: Role inventory-reader exists and already grants get and list on configmaps, so the permission set is adequate.

ruled_out.alternative: The pod is crashing or its script ConfigMap mount is broken.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: ConfigMap inventory-sync-scripts exists with the run.sh key the volume mount needs, and the container started and ran the script.

verification.command: kubectl -n inventory get rolebinding inventory-reader-binding -o jsonpath='{.subjects[0].name}'

verification.must_contain: serviceaccounts that exist in inventory: default, inventory-sync
